text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denies "Bar-On for Hebron" deal. Opposition calls for criminal probe.
- Swiss agree to Holocaust memorial fund.
- Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul Karim Kabariti writes Netanyahu calling for renewed dialogue.
- Business leaders claim privatisation plan lacks depth.
- Union of Local Authorities demands resignation of Treasury, Wages and Labour agreements Director Yossi Kucik following publication of his third annual Public Bodies Salaries Report.
- IDB Holding Corporation will acquire Udi Recanati's share in YLR Capital Markets for about 18.3 million shekels.
GLOBES
- Sharp drop of 0.8 percent in economic activity index in December. Rise in 1996 only 3.7 percent.
- Dollar continues to rise -- to 3.303 shekels. Bank of Israel continues buying foreign currency.
HAARETZ
- U.S. administration exempts American companies from ban on doing business with Syria.
- Body found in sea a month ago -- yeshiva seminary student from South Africa who studied in Jerusalem.
- Bank of Israel official: "Continued growth conditioned on rise in exports."
MAARIV
- Rising opposition to bill that would give Israelis abroad the right to vote.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel and Syria close to joint working paper.
